question: Why does increasing the intensity of incident light increase the photoelectric current but not the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons, provided the frequency is above threshold frequency?

options.A: Increasing intensity increases $K_{\max}$ because the energy of each photon becomes larger.
options.B: Increasing intensity decreases $K_{\max}$ because more photons collide with each other.
options.C: Photoelectric current remains constant because intensity does not affect the number of photons.
options.D: At fixed frequency above threshold, greater intensity means more photons per second, so more electrons are emitted and current increases. Photon energy remains $h\nu$, so $K_{\max}=h\nu-\phi_0$ remains unchanged.
